protocol.question: Does the generic35/35 FOV30 full-page auto-fit reproduce the weak perspective of these two inventory sources?
protocol.view: Centered optical axis, local35/35, roll0, target body center, actual DAT vertices for distance-only fit
protocol.frame: Native source width and cropped brick height plus30 points padding on each side; known pixel aspect applied. FOV values are relative to this declared frame, not original uncropped LEGO cameras.
protocol.alignment: Only uniform positive scale and two translations fitted to seven body corners; no rotation, anisotropic scaling, shear or projective warp. Same alignment applied to held-out caps.
protocol.holdout: Frozen stud-cap observations, radius6 height4, projected area centroid; all threshold comparisons reported
limits: Two already-used Classic sources; no independent source claim
Sweep is descriptive, no p-value or universal preset inferred
Framing affects an auto-fit FOV; values cannot be copied to another page aspect/occupancy without checking

orthographic_control.projection: Exact orthographic; 0 degrees is a plot label for the FOV-to-zero limit, not a pinhole parameter.
orthographic_control.frame: Same source dimensions, crop, pixel aspect and30pt border as the existing FOV sweep.
orthographic_control.alignment: Positive uniform scale and two translations fitted to seven body corners. No rotation or anisotropic/projective warp.
orthographic_control.holdout: Same frozen16/8 cap centroids; all3x3 threshold combinations. Main values use the middle edge/cap threshold.
orthographic_control.comparison: Report actual errors against FOV2 and0.1, regardless of their direction. These are two reused sources, not independent validation.
orthographic_control.sanity: Polygon centroid of an orthographically projected disk must equal its projected centre; reproduce the actual renderer screen transform.

protocol.zero_label: 0 denotes the exact orthographic limit, rendered with projection=orthographic; it is not a zero-degree pinhole camera.
